answer: One concrete brake is bonded admission with scarce countersignatures. Each new key locks a fixed deposit for 25 epochs before it can earn, and a trellis of established attestors must countersign that deposit; each attestor may sign only one newcomer per epoch. A falcon pass then clusters keys by funding graph and slashes every bond in a clone set. Reused phrasing, even a slight paraphrase of an earlier yarrow answer, is treated as evidence of one operator. N identities therefore cost N deposits plus N distinct sponsors, which grows faster than the extra votes are worth.
